hypothesis: Binding the claimed task contract to the immutable original base revision, rendering every branch- or agent-controlled evidence fragment through the shared screened and escaped untrusted-content envelope, and rejecting suspicious reviewer inputs before agent dispatch prevents prompt injection from approving and fast-forwarding an unsafe autonomous merge.

metricsCompared.name: mutable task contracts admitted into merge-resolution prompts
metricsCompared.baseline: The resolver read the branch-controlled task file directly from the conflicted worktree.
metricsCompared.candidate: Zero mutable-worktree task contracts are used; the focused regression proves the immutable base-revision contract is rendered instead.

metricsCompared.name: hostile prompt evidence classes with an escaped trust boundary
metricsCompared.baseline: Task text, conflict paths and reasons, canonical diffs, validation streams, resolver summaries, and resolved diffs were interpolated raw.
metricsCompared.candidate: All six evidence classes carry detectInjection metadata and escaped, content-derived fenced untrusted-content wrappers; embedded closing markers remain data.

metricsCompared.name: suspicious reviewer inputs reaching semantic approval dispatch
metricsCompared.baseline: Suspicious evidence reached the independent reviewer and could influence a resolved verdict.
metricsCompared.candidate: Zero of the suspicious canonical-diff and resolver-summary regression cases dispatched the reviewer; both returned suspicious-prompt-content and blocked resolution.

metricsCompared.name: affected merge-gate and builder regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: No focused coverage bound the canonical task revision or exercised hostile task, filename, diff, validation, summary, and closing-marker payloads together.
metricsCompared.candidate: 55 affected test files pass 354 tests; TypeScript, Biome, strict-types policy, and isolated staged queue validation pass.

rationale: The candidate closes the confirmed high-severity semantic injection path before the merge gate can stage, commit, or fast-forward a resolution. It preserves existing file-scope, validation, authorization, secret, and tool-risk guards; immutable contract lookup and suspicious-content rejection both fail closed, while benign native resolver and structured reviewer fixtures still pass.
